Congo’s Katanga Minerals Unveils New Cobalt Processing Technology

Katanga Minerals Group, one of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) leading mining firms, announced the launch of an advanced cobalt processing system on Monday in Lubumbashi. The launch is expected to bolster the DRC’s role as a key supplier in the global battery metals market and support efforts to increase value-added production within the country.

The new technology, named KobaPure, was developed in partnership with the local engineering firm TechMet Solutions and is designed to increase extraction efficiency and reduce environmental impact during the refining process. Company officials say KobaPure can yield cobalt product purity levels of up to 99.9%, making it particularly attractive to global electric vehicle and energy storage manufacturers.

“By deploying KobaPure at our facilities, we aim not only to meet but to exceed international standards for cobalt quality,” said Katanga Minerals CEO Jean-Paul Kasongo during the unveiling ceremony. “This innovation demonstrates our commitment to responsible mining and to making the DRC a leader in downstream mineral processing.”

Industry analysts note that the DRC currently supplies over 70% of the world’s cobalt, a critical component in lithium-ion batteries. However, much of the raw material has traditionally been exported for processing abroad. Initiatives like KobaPure are seen as significant steps toward retaining more value within the country and creating skilled local jobs.

“Domestic processing is a long-term goal for the DRC’s mining strategy, and technologies like these are essential for achieving it,” said Mireille Tshomba, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Afrique Métaux. “If successful, it could also strengthen the sector’s resilience to global price fluctuations.”

The Congolese Chamber of Mines welcomed the launch, describing it as a “milestone in the modernization of the national mining industry.” In a statement, the Chamber emphasized the importance of continued investment in technology and workforce training.

Katanga Minerals reported that the KobaPure system has already been piloted at its Kolwezi site over the past six months, with production yields exceeding initial targets. The firm plans to expand the technology to all its major operations by year-end.

Shares in Kinshasa-listed miners rose modestly on the news, with the sector index closing up 1.2%. Local officials expressed optimism that the rollout will encourage further innovation and investment in the region.
